aws_elasticsearch_domain.opensearch uses vpc_options, which per the AWS provider requires the Amazon Elasticsearch/OpenSearch service-linked role to exist first. The example conditionally creates aws_iam_service_linked_role.opensearch (aws_service_name "es.amazonaws.com") but the domain has no dependency on it, so on a fresh account domain creation fails. Add depends_on = [aws_iam_service_linked_role.opensearch]. No attribute on the domain can reference the role, so a bare depends_on is the correct fix.

module.emr_on_eks already depends on module.aws_eks implicitly because eks_cluster_id = module.aws_eks.cluster_id references the module. Listing module.aws_eks again in depends_on duplicates that dependency; the depends_on is only needed for kubernetes_config_map.aws_auth.

module.aws_eks_teams passes eks_cluster_id = module.aws_eks.cluster_id, which already establishes an implicit dependency on module.aws_eks. The explicit depends_on = [module.aws_eks] duplicates that dependency and can be removed.

aws_eks_node_group.managed_ng sets node_role_arn = aws_iam_role.managed_ng.arn, which already creates an implicit dependency on that role. Including aws_iam_role.managed_ng again in depends_on is redundant.

null_resource.update_trust_policy already references aws_iam_role.emr_on_eks_execution.id in its local-exec command, establishing an implicit dependency on the role. Listing aws_iam_role.emr_on_eks_execution again in depends_on is redundant.

null_resource.update_trust_policy already references kubernetes_namespace.spark.id in its local-exec command, establishing an implicit dependency on the namespace. Listing kubernetes_namespace.spark again in depends_on is redundant.

aws_eks_addon.aws_ebs_csi_driver sets service_account_role_arn = module.irsa_addon.irsa_iam_role_arn (when the config value is empty), which already creates an implicit dependency on module.irsa_addon. The explicit depends_on = [module.irsa_addon] duplicates it.
